A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoLA-World, with matching authors, core method and retained experiments. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and visually inspected figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original linear-probing, video-prediction, visual-planning and action-transfer results, alongside training and codebook analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds scaling studies, Wan2.1 experiments, expanded planning evaluations and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds a Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B backbone instantiation using the same AdaLN conditioning and warm-up/joint-training procedure. This is a limited model extension; the original OpenSora architecture, latent-action components, objectives and training procedure in Section 3 and Appendix B remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Planning coverage expands from four to seven RoboDesk tasks by adding Push Red, Push Green and Push Blue. Flat Block and Push Drawer remain in Appendix C.3 despite disappearing from the main planning table. The training mixture and simulation datasets remain unchanged; naming the four LIBERO suites adds documentation rather than establishing new coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds previously published AdaWorld planning scores to Tables 3 and 4; v1 only compared its own two-stage and joint models there. Figure 9 also introduces the two-stage baseline into the qualitative action-transfer comparison. Longer-trained checkpoints extend the existing baseline's settings rather than introduce another method.

E3.justification: v2 adds a LAM30K+WM52K control, model-depth and batch-size sweeps with corresponding warm-up schedules, Wan2.1 training configurations, and planning comparisons using 50 versus 200 action candidates and longer-trained checkpoints. These substantially extend the experimental design. Appendix C.3 also specifies planning-only three-step unguided inference, whereas v1 supplies only the general ten-step guided inference setting.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to world-model capacity, training-data exposure, backbone choice, planning sample count and training budget. Appendix D.5 examines computational efficiency, and Figure 9 adds comparative action-transfer case studies. The original warm-up, co-evolution and downstream codebook analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.5 newly states that planning runs use five seeds. v1 describes 30 initial-goal pairs per task but does not disclose a seed count. This establishes additional reporting, not an increase in runs. Neither version reports confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original probing and simulation entries are retained, but planning scores are revised: Upright Block changes from 20.0%/37.78% to 22.00%/35.33% for two-stage/joint models. v2 adds extensive budget, scaling, Wan2.1, runtime and transfer-comparison results. These are newly reported or revised results, not uniform performance gains; planning averages also cover different task sets.

T1.justification: The world-model formulation and reconstruction objective in Equation 1 are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the added scaling and efficiency analyses are empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of warm-up-enabled joint training, synergistic co-evolution, improved efficiency and stronger simulation and planning performance. The conclusion references additional backbone and scaling evidence without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: New discussion connects larger world models with stronger supervision for latent actions and interprets Wan2.1 results as evidence of architectural generality. Appendix D.5 distinguishes higher per-step costs from faster convergence, while C.3 acknowledges a sampling-speed/quality tradeoff. The existing collapse explanation and dependence-on-pretraining limitation remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs, per-step and total training times, planning-specific inference and candidate-count details, and the four LIBERO adaptation suites. It documents configurations for the added studies and replaces the supplementary-folder link with a project website for demos. Core implementation details in Appendix B remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion or citations for UniSkill, Motus, AC-LAM, MVP-LAM, LAWM, FLAM and V-JEPA2-based latent-action modeling, and removes the MaskGIT reference. These sharpen distinctions involving skill discovery, fixed action labels and nongenerative dynamics models while retaining the original joint-training novelty position.

P1.justification: v2 edits terminology and rewrites portions of related work, probing interpretation and evaluation explanations. Appendix D gains three subsections and additional cross-references. Most original prose and the main section hierarchy remain intact; the revision is primarily an empirical expansion.

P2.justification: v2 moves the original probing table into the appendix, expands and restructures planning tables, and adds scaling, backbone and timing tables. It adds a scaling plot and reworks the single transfer gallery into Figures 7–9, including baseline comparisons. Existing Figures 1–5 are retained with resizing or relocation.

improvement.justification: v1 supports efficiency mainly through training-step counts and tests only one backbone. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence with longer-trained controls, reported wall-clock costs, Wan2.1 validation and scaling studies, while expanding planning to all seven tasks. These address important validation gaps. Missing uncertainty estimates and coupled batch-size/warm-up changes still limit interpretation, but the broader controls and clearer reporting provide a substantial net improvement.
